summary: A fast, tight card game where each of the six clan decks plays like a distinct engine-builder, with players racing to chain building bonuses while occasionally raiding or blocking each other's islands. It's lighter and more streamlined than the original Imperial Settlers, with a strong solo/duel feel even at higher player counts.
praised: Six wildly different clan decks give strong replayability and asymmetry
Fast turns and short playtime relative to depth
Satisfying engine-building and combo chaining within a single deck
Good production values and iconography once learned
Works well solo and at 2 players
criticised: Interaction can feel indirect or bolted-on (raiding/exploring) compared to true confrontation
Some clans are noticeably harder to pilot well than others (stated 1-10 difficulty spread)
Iconography-heavy cards have a learning curve
Can feel more solitaire/parallel than the 'Take That' tag suggests, especially at higher player counts
Diminishing tension in the endgame as players optimize known combos

interaction.kind: raiding, blocking islands, and occasional take-that card effects amid mostly parallel engine building

scoring.why: Points accumulate from a mix of building bonuses, raiding/exploration rewards, and end-game scoring cards, but the game ends the instant someone crosses the 25-point threshold, so tempo matters as much as total sources.

_name: Imperial Settlers: Empires of the North
